glossary.Clotting: The process by which blood turns from liquid to a gel to stop bleeding.
glossary.Over-coagulation: Excess anticoagulant effect, so blood clots far less than intended.
glossary.Fetal: Relating to the developing baby in the womb.
glossary.Bruising: Bleeding under the skin, causing purple or blue discolouration.
glossary.GI bleeding: Bleeding anywhere in the gut from mouth to anus.
glossary.Pallor: Unusually pale skin, often a sign of anaemia.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
glossary.Immune-mediated: Caused by the body's own immune system, such as antibodies.
glossary.Platelet: A small blood cell fragment that clumps together to plug bleeding vessels.
glossary.Thrombosis: Formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel.
glossary.Ciprofloxacin: A quinolone antibiotic that inhibits CYP450, raising warfarin levels.
glossary.Omeprazole: A proton pump inhibitor that reduces stomach acid.
glossary.Sodium valproate: An anti-epileptic drug that is also a CYP450 inhibitor.
glossary.Clarithromycin: A macrolide antibiotic that inhibits CYP450 enzymes.
glossary.Fluconazole: An antifungal drug that inhibits CYP450 enzymes.
glossary.Rifampicin: An antibiotic used for TB that strongly induces CYP450 enzymes.
glossary.Phenobarbital: A barbiturate anti-epileptic that induces liver CYP450 enzymes.
glossary.Clinical assessment: Judging a patient's state from history and examination.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin: the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells.
glossary.Reversal: Undoing the effect of a drug, here restoring normal clotting.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.Clotting profile: A set of blood tests (PT, APTT, fibrinogen) showing how well the blood clots.
glossary.Withhold: Temporarily not give a dose of a drug.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given directly into a vein.
glossary.Monoclonal antibody: A laboratory-made antibody that binds one specific target.
glossary.ICH: Intracranial haemorrhage: bleeding inside the skull.
glossary.Overdose: Taking or receiving more of a drug than is safe.
glossary.AF: Atrial fibrillation: an irregular heart rhythm that raises stroke risk.
glossary.DVT: Deep vein thrombosis: a clot in a deep vein, usually of the leg.
glossary.PE: Pulmonary embolism: a clot blocking an artery in the lungs.
glossary.Provoked: Caused by a clear temporary trigger such as surgery or immobility.
glossary.Transfusion: Giving blood or blood products into a vein.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment to keep the patient stable while the underlying problem is fixed.
glossary.Coagulation cascade: The chain of clotting factors activating each other to form a fibrin clot.
glossary.Collagen: A structural protein in vessel walls exposed when they are injured.
glossary.Common pathway: The final shared part of the clotting cascade, from factor X to fibrin.
glossary.Factor Xa: Activated factor X, which converts prothrombin into thrombin.
glossary.Direct thrombin inhibitor: A drug that binds and blocks thrombin itself.
glossary.Clotting factors: Proteins in the blood that work in sequence to form a clot.
glossary.Precursors: Inactive forms of a molecule that need modifying before they work.
glossary.Haemostatic balance: The balance between clotting and bleeding in the blood.
glossary.Antibodies: Proteins made by the immune system that bind specific targets.
glossary.Platelet consumption: Using up platelets faster than they are made, as they are used in clots.
